title: Space Tech Briefing — September 17, 2026
summary:
Good morning, space enthusiasts and future voyagers! This is your daily orbital update, live on this magnificent **September 17, 2026**! We're kicking off today with some truly out-of-this-world news, from orbital defense to Martian exploration and a look back at Europe's ambitious space summit!

First up, straight from the French space agency CNES: France is getting serious about protecting its assets in orbit! And no, it's not a green, big-eared Jedi Master, but a sophisticated system named **Yoda** that France is now relying on to defend its satellites. This isn't science fiction, folks; this is the reality of safeguarding national interests in the increasingly crowded expanse of space. Yoda is poised to be a crucial player in maintaining France's orbital security. We'll be keeping a close eye on this guardian of the galaxy – the French version, that is!

Next up, mark your calendars for an exciting journey to the Red Planet's neighborhood! The **MMX mission**, or Martian Moons eXploration, is gearing up for launch. Led by Japan, this groundbreaking mission is scheduled to blast off on **October 19, 2026**. Its target? Mars' enigmatic moons, Phobos and Deimos. The goal is to conduct an in-depth study of these celestial bodies, potentially revealing secrets about the formation of our solar system. And guess what? France’s CNES is making significant contributions to this incredible international endeavor. Get ready for some close-up lunar views – Martian lunar views, that is!

And as we look forward to those incredible launches, let's take a quick look back at a pivotal event that just wrapped up. Just last week, on **September 9th and 10th, 2026**, Paris played host to the very first International Space Summit. This landmark event, initiated by French President Emmanuel Macron and co-chaired by France and Germany, gathered states, agencies, industry leaders, and startups from a sector now valued at over 500 billion dollars! The summit, held at the Grand Palais, saw major announcements including significant new investments and the exciting news of Europe's first-ever Greek astronaut. It was a clear signal of Europe's ambition to truly scale up its presence in space, even as it highlighted some of the continent's ongoing challenges. A truly defining moment for European space strategy!

And that’s your morning briefing from the final frontier! Thank you for tuning in and staying connected to the incredible world of space technology. Keep looking up, and we'll catch you next time!
